text:
**What a crash can lose.** The durability mode decides when a commit is acknowledged relative to the WAL sync. It is a setting of the process that opens the store (`--durability-mode` or `RELATE_DURABILITY_MODE`, default `full`), not of the store.

The picture's timeline: 8 writes are acknowledged in the 4.6 s after a completed checkpoint, then the process crashes. A killed process can lose the window as well as a power cut.

| Mode | The WAL is synced | Acknowledged writes the crash at 4.6 s can lose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `full` | Before each commit, or group of commits, is acknowledged | None: all 8 come back |
| `everysecond` | About once a second, in the background | The 2 writes after the last sync, at 4 s |
| `snapshot` | Never on commit; only a completed checkpoint is durable | All 8, every write since the checkpoint |

Under `everysecond`, slow storage or a delayed sync makes the window longer than about a second. Under `snapshot`, the window runs until the next completed checkpoint: up to 300 seconds of writes under the default timer, fewer when a WAL segment fills first.
